42: I am too barbarous to be human, of minute wisdom—how could I begin to argue with a great master of the Torah, from whom it has no secrets and to whom all its mysteries are clear as glass, the great and powerful tree of knowledge, the mighty hammer, my teacher the great Rabbi Solomon. So [instead] I come to prostrate myself before my teacher from afar and to entreat him to explain these Torah matters which are too secreted for me to understand.
And now, my dear teacher, to make known to your honored self how Reuben came to me and accused Simon . . .

. . . Enlighten us with clear arguments, and may the Princes of Light accompany you, and may God grant you joy and song and life and peace. So sends your student, your footstool, Elijah ben Aaron the Master. The ignoramus writes as he can, but your majesty is beyond description.
